messages.author: fcb0ae32a25dfb37
messages.subject: lavaan with three nominal variable
parts:
Hi all,

I am doing some SEM analysis with three nominal variables (Forage type:CM, SF, and compare with the baseline BM).  in the book, it is said "If you have a nominal categorical variable with $K > 2$ levels, you need to replace it by a set of $K-1$ dummy variables, again, just like you would do in classical regression"
I am not sure whether I am doing it the right way. What I did is set it with two dummy variables, Forage 1, and Forage 2. So in Forage.1 cm=1, sf=0, bm=0, in Forage.2, cm=0,sf=1,bm=0. Then when fitting the model " model1 <- '
  
  NH4.N~Period.daily.Rainfall+Air.Temp+Forage.1+Forage.2
  NO3.N~Period.daily.Rainfall+Air.Temp+Forage.1+Forage.2
 yield~NH4.N+NO3.N+Period.daily.Rainfall+Air.Temp+Forage.1+Forage.2+topography index".

So in the end, what is the coefficient number from Forage.1 and Forage .2 to the yield means?

messages.author: 5b9c62b1c7cbc1e6
messages.subject: Re: lavaan with three nominal variable
parts:
You don't say what book you mean by "in the book," but that is the most common way to code a nominal predictor in regression, yes. The coefficient for Forage.1 in the first equation, for example, would be the model-implied difference in NH4.N between "cm" and "bm" (the 0/0 group, or reference group) holding Period.daily.Rainfall and Air.Temp constant.

Here, that might be what you want, as "bm" is a baseline. Assuming you're working in significance-testing framework, I also generally recommend testing with a multiple-df test (either Wald or likelihood ratio) constraining the coefficients of Forage.1 and Forage.2 to zero simultaneously, as that is the test of "no effect of forage type."

All that said, since you're operating in an SEM package, you have the option of treating the three levels of forage as a grouping variable and running a multiple-group model, which would give you more flexibility. There are examples in the lavaan tutorials for the syntax, and in any SEM reference (e.g., Kline's textbook free online) for the logic.

Pat
